featured.title: US–Iran Tensions Keep Global Energy Markets on Alert
featured.content: The confrontation between the United States and Iran remains one of the world's biggest geopolitical risks. President Donald Trump has warned that the US could target Iran's fortified Pickaxe Mountain, while disruption around the Strait of Hormuz continues to affect energy markets. Oil prices have climbed sharply as investors assess the possibility of a wider regional escalation.

articles.title: BREAKING: Trump Warns Iran's Pickaxe Mountain Could Be Targeted
articles.description: President Donald Trump said the United States could strike Iran's Pickaxe Mountain very soon. The fortified site near the damaged Natanz nuclear facility contains deeply buried tunnel complexes, making any attack potentially significant for the wider conflict.
articles.imageQuery: Iran Pickaxe Mountain Natanz nuclear facility

articles.title: Iran Nuclear Dispute Moves Toward International Escalation
articles.description: The United States, Britain, France and Germany are pushing the International Atomic Energy Agency board towards referring Iran to the United Nations Security Council over concerns about its nuclear programme. Diplomatic efforts remain possible, but tensions are high.

articles.title: Strait of Hormuz Remains a Global Energy Flashpoint
articles.description: Shipping through the Strait of Hormuz remains severely disrupted as the US–Iran confrontation continues. The uncertainty is supporting higher oil prices and increasing concerns about fuel supplies and inflation around the world.

articles.title: Russia Strikes Ukraine Security Service Headquarters
articles.description: A Russian drone struck the headquarters of Ukraine's Security Service in central Kyiv, one of the most prominent government targets hit during the war. At least 12 people were reported injured, while Ukrainian officials warned of a possible response.
articles.imageQuery: Kyiv SBU headquarters Russian drone attack

articles.title: US Envoys Prepare Ukraine Peace Mission
articles.description: US representatives Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner are preparing to travel to Moscow and Kyiv as Washington seeks a path towards ending the Russia–Ukraine war. No peace agreement has been reached.
articles.imageQuery: Ukraine Russia peace talks US envoy

articles.title: Two Nepal Flood Survivors Rescued After Nine Days
articles.description: Two hydropower workers were rescued alive from a flooded tunnel in Nepal nine days after catastrophic flooding swept through the Trishuli River valley. Their rescue has renewed hope for other workers still missing.

articles.title: Nepal Disaster Leaves More Than 1,250 Dead
articles.description: Nepal continues a massive humanitarian and rescue operation following catastrophic flooding and landslides. More than 1,250 people have died, while thousands remain missing as rescue teams search damaged hydropower facilities and communities.

articles.title: Washington Considers Further Action Against Iran
articles.description: The Trump administration is considering additional military action against Iran as tensions remain high. Any further escalation could have consequences for regional security, shipping and global energy prices.

articles.title: US Investors Move Toward Safer Assets
articles.description: Investors are becoming more cautious as geopolitical tensions, higher oil prices and elevated government bond yields create uncertainty. US equity funds recorded another weekly outflow while money-market funds attracted strong inflows.

articles.title: US Government Debt Remains a Major Economic Issue
articles.description: High government borrowing and rising bond yields continue to raise questions about the long-term cost of servicing US debt and the effect of fiscal pressures on financial markets.

articles.title: Europe Watches Middle East Energy Risks
articles.description: European economies remain exposed to the consequences of higher energy prices and prolonged Middle East instability. Investors are closely monitoring oil, inflation and government borrowing costs.

articles.title: European Migration Policy Remains Under Debate
articles.description: Several European governments are examining new arrangements for managing migration and returns, including possible facilities outside the European Union. The proposals remain politically sensitive.

articles.title: European Bond Yields Remain Under Pressure
articles.description: Higher government borrowing costs are affecting European financial markets as investors reassess inflation, fiscal deficits and the possibility of further central-bank rate increases.

articles.title: BREAKING: SEC Approves Dangote Refinery IPO
articles.description: Nigeria's Securities and Exchange Commission has approved the initial public offering of Dangote Group's refinery business. The offering could raise about ₦2.15 trillion, or $1.63 billion, if fully subscribed.

articles.title: Dangote Refinery IPO Set for September 14
articles.description: The planned offering involves 4.1 billion ordinary shares priced at ₦525 each, according to the company and Reuters. The order book is expected to open on September 14, making it potentially Africa's biggest-ever share sale.

articles.title: Dangote Plans Major Refinery Capacity Expansion
articles.description: Funds from the IPO are expected to support plans to expand the refinery's capacity from 650,000 barrels per day towards 1.4 million barrels per day.

articles.title: Nigeria Could Attract More Energy Investment
articles.description: International Energy Agency chief Fatih Birol says Nigeria could potentially double energy investment within five years as global energy supply disruptions increase demand for reliable oil, gas and renewable-energy partners.

articles.title: Nigeria's Economy Continues to Face Security and Cost Pressures
articles.description: Nigeria's stronger economic growth is being accompanied by continuing challenges involving security, fuel prices, household costs and the need to attract long-term investment.

articles.title: Global Money-Market Funds Attract $46.1 Billion
articles.description: Global money-market funds received a net $46.1 billion in the week ending September 2, their biggest weekly inflow since early August. Investors are seeking safer and more liquid assets amid geopolitical and bond-market uncertainty.

articles.title: Oil Prices Remain Elevated as Hormuz Risks Persist
articles.description: Brent crude climbed sharply during the week as renewed US–Iran tensions increased fears of further disruption around the Strait of Hormuz. Higher energy prices are also adding to inflation concerns.

articles.title: Global Bond Sell-Off Raises Borrowing Costs
articles.description: Government bond yields have climbed across several major economies, increasing borrowing costs for governments, businesses and households while creating new challenges for financial markets.

articles.title: Nvidia Agrees to Buy Hugging Face for $12.93 Billion
articles.description: Nvidia has agreed to acquire AI developer platform Hugging Face for about $12.93 billion. The deal would deepen Nvidia's position in the open-source artificial-intelligence ecosystem.

articles.title: AI Chip Demand Drives South Korean Exports
articles.description: South Korea's exports have reached $709.4 billion so far in 2026, already surpassing the previous full-year record. Semiconductor exports rose 169.6% from a year earlier and now account for 41% of total exports.
articles.imageQuery: South Korea semiconductor factory AI chips

articles.title: South Korea Could Reach $1 Trillion in Annual Exports
articles.description: South Korea is on course to potentially reach $1 trillion in annual exports by early December as strong global demand for artificial-intelligence chips continues to support the country's technology sector.

articles.title: AI Investment Continues to Reshape Global Industry
articles.description: Artificial intelligence is driving demand for advanced chips, computing infrastructure and data centres, with the technology boom increasingly influencing trade, investment and industrial policy.

articles.title: Sydney Faces Extreme Bushfire Risk
articles.description: Sydney is experiencing an unusually intense spring heatwave, with temperatures reaching around 33°C. Authorities have issued an extreme bushfire-risk rating and a total fire ban for the Greater Sydney Region.

articles.title: Typhoon Saudel Brings Flooding to Southern China
articles.description: Typhoon Saudel has brought torrential rain and flooding to parts of southern China. More than 83,000 people have been evacuated in Fujian, while authorities continue emergency operations.

articles.title: China Reports Fresh Landslide Rescue Operation
articles.description: More than 10 people were reported trapped after a landslide struck a town in China's Jiangxi province. Rescue teams are responding as authorities assess the situation.

articles.title: Nordic Football Federations Raise FIFA Governance Concerns
articles.description: Football associations from Nordic countries are seeking greater transparency and consultation in FIFA decision-making and have called for wider European engagement on football governance.

morningSummary.title: MORNING SUMMARY
morningSummary.description: The global picture this Saturday is dominated by conflict, energy security, humanitarian emergencies, extreme weather and technology. US–Iran tensions remain extremely high after President Donald Trump warned that the United States could target Iran's Pickaxe Mountain. The confrontation continues to affect the Strait of Hormuz and global oil markets. In Ukraine, a Russian drone struck the SBU security service headquarters in central Kyiv as US diplomats prepare further peace efforts. Nepal is still dealing with a catastrophic flood disaster, but two hydropower workers were rescued alive after nine days underground. In Nigeria, the Securities and Exchange Commission has approved the Dangote Refinery IPO, potentially creating Africa's biggest-ever share sale. Sydney faces extreme bushfire conditions, while South Korea's AI-driven semiconductor exports have pushed the country's exports beyond its previous annual record. Nvidia's planned $12.93 billion acquisition of Hugging Face is another major sign of the continuing expansion of the global AI industry.

bigQuestion: With wars, rising energy costs, extreme weather and rapid technological change affecting ordinary people at the same time, are governments doing enough to protect citizens from the consequences?
quoteOfTheDay: You cannot control every storm around you, but you can choose to remain informed, prepared and courageous through it.
